About this record

Security Council Record is an independent, non-commercial overlay on the public documentation of the United Nations Security Council. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the United Nations.

Sources

  • Corpus of Resolutions: UN Security Council (CR-UNSC), Seán Fobbe, Lorenzo Gasbarri and Niccolò Ridi, version 2026-08-19, CC0. Texts and metadata of resolutions 1 to 2815, derived from the UN Digital Library.
  • Machine-readable Security Council resolutions (AKN4UN XML), United Nations. Texts and metadata of resolutions adopted after January 2026. The United Nations is the source of this information.
  • UNSC votes since 1946 database, Benoît Martin, Sciences Po Atelier de cartographie and GRAM, 2026, CC BY 4.0. Every recorded vote, including vetoed and failed drafts, 1946 to 2025.
  • Official documents: the Security Council website, the UN Digital Library and the Repertoire of the Practice of the Security Council.

Method

Eras follow political breaks. The opening events are history; every figure is computed from the documents.

Terms such as "threat to the peace", "act of aggression" or "Acting under Chapter VII" are counted with text patterns that allow for scanning errors, and checked by hand on samples. A count means the phrase appears in the text, not necessarily as a formal finding; "breach of the peace" is counted only where the Council determines or states that a breach exists.

Themes (women, children, civilians and others) mark resolutions whose text mentions the subject.

Regions come from the resolution title: the region of the situation it concerns. Admissions, elections and appointments are "institutional"; general subjects are "thematic".

Votes come from the Sciences Po database. Unanimous means every member present voted yes. A contested vote is one with any no vote or abstention, or a draft that failed. Vetoes are counted as no votes by permanent members on vetoed drafts, so a draft vetoed by two members counts for both. China's seat was held by the Republic of China until October 1971; the Soviet seat passed to the Russian Federation in December 1991.

Citations between resolutions come from the CR-UNSC citation network.

Corrections and reuse

This site, its data and its code are in the public domain. Errors in the underlying documents are reproduced as published; spotted a problem in ours? Write to daniel.desposito@gmail.com.

Security Council Record is an independent record of every resolution, vote and veto of the United Nations Security Council since 1946. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the United Nations. For official documents, use the Security Council website and the UN Digital Library.

Built on the documentation of the Security Council, the CR-UNSC corpus (Fobbe, Gasbarri and Ridi, CC0), the UN machine-readable resolutions and the UNSC votes since 1946 database (Sciences Po Atelier de cartographie and GRAM, CC BY 4.0). Method and sources.

Made by Daniel D'Esposito. Designed to work on any phone and with screen readers. Content in the public domain.
